newsitem.title: USA: Dole returns to economic theme in Chicago appearance.
newsitem.headline: Dole returns to economic theme in Chicago appearance.

text.p: Republican candidate Bob Dole returned to his central economic and anti-drug messages as he dove into the Midwest on Wednesday, avoiding the negative themes about President Clinton that emerged a day earlier.
Indeed when a riled up supporter at a Chicago event demanded to know when Dole would take off the "kid gloves" against the Democratic president, Dole didn't take the bait.
"There's a very fine line because there's a myth out there that Bob Dole is mean," Dole replied calmly. "I never thought I was mean."
"He may have a few surprises come next Wednesday," he said, referring to his second scheduled debate with Clinton.

At the Acme Screw Co. in Chicago, Dole met with a pre-selected group of small business owners, including many women, an apparent attempt to close the gender gap that is a major factor in Clinton's lead in the polls.

Dole, who had stressed on Tuesday his trustworthiness versus what he said was Clinton's record of broken and empty promises, handled questions from the audience that enabled him to repeat his standard positions on tax cuts, education, balancing the budget, fighting drugs and helping small businesses.
Even when invited, he did not attack Clinton's character, or attack his record as vigorously as he did Tuesday, including one reference to the president as a "bozo."

Spokesman Nelson Warfield told reporters aboard Dole's campaign jet that the campaign had not made any strategic decisions to go negative on Tuesday, and that too much had been made out of a few remarks.
"He (Dole) had an opportunity in the first debate to delve into President Clinton's personal life, and he chose not to," Warfield said.

"I think he'll be consistent about that," Warfield added. "Throughout the campaign he has avoided personal attacks about the president's personal life and I think he is going to consistently do that."

Forced to cancel half of his campaign appearances in New Jersey on Tuesday because of bad weather, Dole had a light campaign schedule on Wednesday considering that the election is a month away and he is behind in the polls.

He did one radio talk show interview and worked in his Washington office on Wednesday morning, then flew to Chicago, where he scheduled two events scheduled late in the day before watching the vice presidential debate at night.
He was scheduled to campaign in Illinois and Ohio through Friday. The two states together have 43 electoral college votes and are considered key battlegrounds.
